The learner asks specifically: Make sure one of the senses is this meaning: usually; most of the time.

notes: When placed before a verb at the start of a clause, it is very often followed by مَا (غَالِبًا مَا + verb).

senses.definition: In most cases; most of the time.

examples.text: غَالِبًا مَا أَذْهَبُ إِلَى العَمَلِ مَشْيًا.
examples.translation: I usually go to work on foot.

examples.text: يَحْدُثُ هَذَا الخَطَأُ غَالِبًا فِي الشِّتَاءِ.
examples.translation: This error often happens in the winter.

notes: This word is derived from the root g-l-b, which implies 'overcoming' or 'predominance'. Thus, 'ghaliban' literally describes a state where something 'predominantly' occurs.
It is much more common than the word 'katheeran' (often) when you want to express a statistical likelihood or a habit rather than just a high frequency.

senses.definition: Most of the time; in the majority of cases.

examples.text: غالبًا ما أذهب إلى العمل مشيًا.
examples.translation: I usually go to work on foot.
examples.emotion: matter-of-fact and routine, describing a daily habit
examples.note: Note the use of 'ma' after the adverb; this is a common construction to connect the adverb to the following verb phrase.

examples.text: يحدث هذا الخطأ غالبًا في فصل الشتاء.
examples.translation: This error often happens in the winter.
examples.emotion: analytical and objective, explaining a recurring technical issue

faults.why: 'Usually' and 'often' are translations of one meaning ('in most cases'), not distinct Arabic senses.
The essential construction غَالِبًا مَا + verb is buried in an example note instead of notes.
